summary: The draft is unusually evidence-dense and carries most of the load-bearing verbatim quotes (SNGP 'not distance aware', Demsar 'much less than 30', Moosbauer OFAT, Carrete 0.90/0.91, Okada +0.054 to +0.005, the Figure A.7 legend tokens, the four-corner eta-squared table with CIs, the frozen cells to the seed). Twelve places remain where the vault holds sharper, more specific, or more calibrated substance than the draft uses. The two most consequential are in deliverable (iii) RANK 1 -- the centerpiece of the report -- where the draft asserts an unqualified ML-benchmarking novelty claim that its own interim note explicitly warns is contestable, and reports a one-corner simple-effects result where the note supplies a four-corner bootstrapped table. No interim note is ignored wholesale; all six are represented in the draft.

findings.location: (iii) Scope of Novelty, RANK 1, the 'Precedent check' paragraph ending 'No ML benchmark study reports and interprets a component-by-component interaction - verified across three independent regions.'
findings.issue: The draft states the unqualified version of a novelty claim that the depth-investigator explicitly flagged as the contestable version, and drops the sharper framing the note recommends. This is the report's centerpiece finding, so the weaker formulation is where a reviewer will push.
findings.evidence: interim-report-interaction-grounding.md, section (c): 'So the precise, defensible claim is not "no one in ML has ever reported an interaction term." It is: interaction-term reporting is standard, expected practice within the exact fANOVA lineage this paper's own design descends from - just never between "which surrogate model class" and "which search/optimizer strategy" as two independently manipulated pipeline components.' The note anchors this with a number: the vault's Hutter et al. 2014 note 'records 20 grep hits for "interaction"' - e.g. 'interaction effect between S and kappa' - because fANOVA decomposes into main effects AND pairwise interactions by construction. It further establishes that van Rijn & Hutter 2018 'analyzes each algorithm's space in isolation (SVM, then RF, then Adaboost, never jointly), never crossing model class against optimizer.' The note calls the sharper version 'a strictly stronger framing than a bare novelty claim.'
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the precedent claim in the note's form. Concede up front that interaction reporting is routine inside the fANOVA lineage the paper's design descends from -- citing the 20 'interaction' hits in Hutter et al. 2014 [3], which the draft already cites as a near-miss but never credits with this -- and add van Rijn & Hutter's per-algorithm-in-isolation pattern. Then state the residual: never between surrogate model class and search routine as two independently manipulated pipeline components. Keep the Schmidt / Choi / Steiner zero-hit evidence, which supports the narrowed claim unchanged.

findings.location: (i) B2, 'The LCB-paralysis citation inverts the source's central result - the most serious item in this deliverable', the sentence beginning 'Decisively, their Theorem 1 proves MinUCB converges at a polynomial rate...'
findings.issue: The draft's self-declared most serious miscitation finding paraphrases the theorem it convicts Fan with, while quoting Fan verbatim two paragraphs earlier for the much lighter B1 item. The convicting evidence is the least quoted evidence in the section.
findings.evidence: research/temp/evidence-digest.md lines 107-108 hold the verbatim: 'According to Theorem 1, we need to iteratively increase the UCB coefficient beta_t and batch size b(1)t, b(2)t to guarantee the convergence of MinUCB.' (Section 6, lines 415-417) and the rate itself from the Theorem 1 statement (lines 392-397): 'MinUCB will achieve the convergence rate of O(sigma d^(3/2) T^(-1/2) log^(1/2) delta^(-1))'. The digest also records the increasing *batch size* schedule as a second offline-impossible precondition, which the draft compresses to 'continual active resampling'.
findings.recommendation: Quote the 'we need to iteratively increase the UCB coefficient beta_t and batch size' sentence directly, with its section/line locator, and give the rate O(sigma d^(3/2) T^(-1/2) log^(1/2) delta^(-1)) rather than 'a polynomial rate'. Name both offline-impossible preconditions -- the increasing beta schedule AND the growing batch size / per-iteration resampling -- since two independent structural impossibilities is a stronger convictions than one.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 1b, 'Report the formal simple-effects table. Free.'
findings.issue: The draft reports one corner of a four-corner bootstrapped table, gives a CI for only one of three cells, and states the simple-effects methodological requirement with no citation at all -- in a report whose entire subject is citation fidelity.
findings.evidence: interim-report-interaction-grounding.md section (b) supplies the full table with CIs across all four corners: off/off 0.004 [0.001,0.40] | 0.666 [0.48,0.94] | 0.814 [0.64,0.99]; on/off 0.004 [0.001,0.026] | 0.388 [0.16,0.90] | 0.763 [0.53,0.99]; off/on 0.020 [0.004,0.70] | 0.790 [0.61,0.98] | 0.813 [0.64,0.99]; on/on (primary) 0.007 [0.001,0.048] | 0.735 [0.50,0.98] | 0.762 [0.53,0.99] -- with a footnote that the two X1-off corners retain the target-scaling confound, which is why their CIs are wide. The same note supplies the missing methodological citations: Statistics LibreTexts / Kansas State EDCEP 917 section 3.4, verbatim 'Whenever an interaction is detected, researchers need to conduct additional analyses to determine where that interaction is coming from', and the exact 3x3 match 'a researcher using a 3x3 design with nine conditions would need to look at 2 main effects and 6 simple effects' -- which the draft uses as an unattributed fact. And NIST/SEMATECH section 5.4.7.1: 'Note that large interactions can obscure main effects.'
findings.recommendation: Give the effect at all four corners (the perturbation column is 0.004-0.020 everywhere, the gradient/CMA columns 0.388-0.814), which shows the simple-effects asymmetry is corner-invariant like the interaction itself. Carry the CIs for all three cells at the primary corner, not just perturbation. Attribute the '2 main effects and 6 simple effects' figure and the 'main effects can mislead' premise to the LibreTexts and NIST 5.4.7.1 sources, both fetched and quote-verified this session, and add them to the source list.

findings.location: (i)/N6 section D, 'The uncomfortable finding', the sentence 'yields a loss axis at eta-squared ~ 0.027 against a method axis at eta-squared ~ 0.577'
findings.issue: The draft reports two of five numbers from its own from-scratch ANOVA on RaM's Table 3, omits the per-task ranges that show how variable the split is, and drops a fact from RaM's Appendix E.5 that materially strengthens the paper's residual.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n6-residual-scoping-legitimate-or-gerrymandered.md section (d): 'eta-squared_Method (the method/optimizer axis) = 0.577 [range 0.134-0.958 across tasks], eta-squared_Loss = 0.027 [range 0.0004-0.076], eta-squared_Method x Loss interaction = 0.055, eta-squared_within = 0.341.' Separately, from RaM's own Appendix E.5, the note records that 'COMs, RoMA, IOM, BDI, and ICT were excluded from the swap because their losses use prediction values or per-sample weights incompatible with a drop-in MSE-to-ListNet replacement - the crossing is an opportunistic subset of offline-MBO methods, not an exhaustive design.'
findings.recommendation: Add the interaction term (0.055) and the within-cell residual (0.341) so the decomposition is complete and a reader can see it sums, and give the per-task ranges [0.134-0.958] and [0.0004-0.076] so the 0.027-vs-0.577 contrast is not read as a stable constant. Add the exclusion fact -- RaM could only cross the five methods whose losses admit a drop-in swap -- as an independent structural point in favour of the residual: the crossing is opportunistic, not designed, which is exactly the difference the paper is claiming.

findings.location: (i) M, 'Five other cells tie it should be six' paragraph, and section N's 'Frozen cells, to the seed' row; also the opening verdict's list 'the inversion counts'
findings.issue: The draft's only concrete inversion number is the one that FAILS to reproduce. The three counts that do reproduce -- and which form a monotone ladder across surrogate class -- appear nowhere, so the section reads as a recount dispute rather than as a verification pass with one exception.
findings.evidence: research/temp/local-checks.md L2.7 verifies against results/x0_inversion.json (git_sha 9843dfc8, X1/X3 both on): 'ensemble inverts on >=1 optimizer on 7/7 tasks - 7/7 (all seven)'; 'SVGP 3/7 (Branin, Rastrigin, Styblinski)'; 'exact GP 2/7 (Rastrigin, Styblinski)'; plus 'Branin-2D ens:grad inversion_rate 1.0' and 'mean_frac_worse 1.0'. All marked verified exactly.
findings.recommendation: State the verified ladder -- ensemble 7/7, SVGP 3/7, exact GP 2/7, with the named tasks -- before the off-by-one, so the recount lands as the single exception in a passing sweep rather than as the section's only data point. The ordering is also independent corroboration of the paper's surrogate-axis result on a completely different statistic, which is worth a clause.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 6, 'The landscape negative', the clause 'Separability fares no better.'
findings.issue: A three-word dismissal stands where the interim note has a quantified contrast that is more striking than the multimodality result the draft does report, plus a self-refuted alternative hypothesis that makes the whole negative more defensible.
findings.evidence: interim-report-landscape-predicts-which-surrogate-wins.md Finding 3: from the oracle formulas, 'Styblinski, Levy, and Rastrigin are separable... while Branin, Rosenbrock, Ackley, and Griewank are not; the separable group's gaps (2.09-21.20, ~10x) span a *narrower* range than the non-separable group's (0.19-2591, ~13,600x), which contains both the extreme minimum and the extreme maximum.' Finding 4 adds a refuted hypothesis of the investigator's own: 'I read code/mbo.py directly and found each oracle applies an affine map from the shared [0,1]^d design space back to that function's exact native textbook domain (Branin -> x1 in [-5,10], x2 in [0,15]; Styblinski -> [-5,5]; Levy -> [-10,10]; Rastrigin -> [-5.12,5.12]; Griewank -> [-600,600]...). The domain-flattening hypothesis is false; the tasks really do sit on their standard, well-characterized landscapes, which makes the non-result... stronger, not weaker.' Finding 2 gives the cross-optimizer stability with pairings and p-values: 0.84 grad-pert (p=0.019), 0.96 grad-cma (p<0.001), 0.91 pert-cma (p=0.005).
findings.recommendation: Replace 'Separability fares no better' with the 10x-versus-13,600x span contrast, which is the sharper form of the same negative. Add one clause recording that the tasks were verified from code/mbo.py to sit on their exact native textbook domains, so the null is not an artifact of a flattening reparametrization -- this pre-empts the obvious reviewer rescue of the landscape hypothesis. Attach the pairings and p-values to the '0.84-0.96' stability range rather than leaving it as a bare interval.

findings.location: Missing entirely -- belongs in (i) E (the li2024bnnsurrogates item) or (iii) RANK 6
findings.issue: The vault holds a direct, citable tension between a load-bearing cited paper's stated expectation and this paper's own data, and the report never uses it. This is squarely the deliverable-(i) question ('does the literature CONTRADICT any claim') and the deliverable-(iii) 'under-explained' question, and it involves the same source the report already convicts on the K-range.
findings.evidence: interim-report-landscape-predicts-which-surrogate-wins.md, 'What the corpus already said': Li, Rudner & Wilson (ICLR 2024) state in their own abstract 'the ranking of methods is highly problem dependent, suggesting the need for tailored inductive biases,' and their body names dimensionality and non-stationarity as the drivers -- 'GPs do not scale well to high-dimensional input spaces without careful human intervention... BNN surrogates can learn the non-stationarity of the function.' The note records that this 'predicts GPs should *lose* ground in high dimensions, which is not what this paper's own data shows,' against a measured dimension-gap Spearman of 0.107 / -0.109 / 0.071, indistinguishable from zero under all three optimizers. Lim et al. 2021, surfaced by a sibling locus, points the same way as this paper ('even the most complex high-dimensional dataset... GP becomes the top performer').
findings.recommendation: Add this as a short item: the closest prior surrogate-class comparison predicts, qualitatively, that the GP advantage should decay with dimension; this paper's own seven-task data shows no dimension relationship in either direction under any optimizer. That is a measured, falsifiable refinement of a named prior expectation -- the same shape of contribution the report praises in the Fannjiang item (i.J) -- and it strengthens rather than weakens the paper's use of li2024bnnsurrogates elsewhere.

findings.location: (i) N, the 'Code-level line traces for Confounds 1 and 2' row: 'PASS without exception. Every claimed line resolves to exactly what the paper says; lines 35-40 of mbo.py are a source comment stating the defect in *more* detail than the paper does'
findings.issue: The draft's own front-matter says the audit's most falsifiable class of claim passes, then gives the reader nothing to check. The brief named the mbo.py line traces as a depth target; the vault has the line-by-line table and the verbatim comment.
findings.evidence: research/temp/local-checks.md L2.5 gives the Confound 1 trace line by line -- line 34 'X1_STANDARDIZE_Y = os.environ.get("MBO_X1","1") != "0"'; 157-162 'if X1_STANDARDIZE_Y: ym, ys = y.mean(), y.std()+1e-8; y_fit = (y-ym)/ys else: ym, ys, y_fit = 0.0, 1.0, y' (ensemble trains on RAW y when X1 off); 293 'normalize_y=True, alpha=1e-6' and 379-381 'ym, ys = yt.mean(), yt.std()+1e-8' (both GPs standardize) -- and the verbatim Confound 2 comment at lines 35-40: 'Pre-audit, grad returned the final iterate of all 2*TOP inits and perturb the per-slot best of 2*TOP, while cma returned top-TOP by surrogate LCB -- so grad/perturb spent 2x cma's ORACLE budget and eval_designs' oracle top-k made p50 a top-half median for two optimizers and a full-set median for the third. Two estimands, one column.' The note records that the paper's phrase 'two estimands in one column' is lifted from its own source comment, 'which is fair.' It also records an incidental corroboration: 'line 293 is a scikit-learn GP and 379-381 a torch GP, two distinct GP implementations in one file. That independently supports the paper's separate disclosure that the premise-coverage value of 0.97 in the prior analysis belongs to a scikit-learn exact GP, not the differentiable GP the grid scores.'
findings.recommendation: Quote the 'Two estimands, one column' comment in full and note that the paper's own phrasing is lifted from it. Give at least the two decisive Confound 1 lines (157-162 ensemble-on-raw-y versus 293 / 379-381 both-GPs-standardize) so a reader can verify the asymmetry claim in one open-file. Add the two-GP-implementations observation where the report uses the 0.97 premise-coverage figure (RANK 1a), since it independently corroborates a disclosure the paper makes.

findings.location: Opening verdict, 'the pessimism increment with its paired-delta and z-score cross-check', and (i) M, 'Three presentation gaps invite false arithmetic catches'
findings.issue: The draft claims Elimination 1's seven figures reproduced and then shows only the one that looks like an arithmetic error. The remaining six -- including an internal cross-check on a completely different scale that lands on the same ratio -- are the evidence for the 'severity to the results is NIL' thesis, and they are asserted rather than shown.
findings.evidence: research/temp/local-checks.md L2a table verifies, paper against artifact results/beta0_reconcile.json: beta=0 gap '0.319 [0.196,0.460]' vs 0.31922 [0.19636, 0.45950]; beta=2 gap '0.525 [0.406,0.614]' vs 0.52519 [0.40641, 0.61389]; increment '0.203 [0.007,0.396]', p=0.020 vs 0.20321 [0.00716, 0.39552], p=0.0204; z-score cross-check '0.904' vs '1.473' against 0.90374, 1.47272; 'the same 0.61 ratio' against 0.319/0.525 = 0.608 and 0.904/1.473 = 0.614; Branin per-task beta=0 0.664 vs 0.46821; Griewank beta=0 0.098 vs 0.09845.
findings.recommendation: Show the two gaps with their intervals (0.319 [0.196,0.460] and 0.525 [0.406,0.614]) alongside the paired delta, which also makes the 0.206-subtraction trap self-explanatory. Add the z-score cross-check numbers (0.904 / 1.473 -> 0.614 against 0.608 on the raw scale): an independent recomputation on a different normalization landing within 0.006 of the same ratio is the strongest single piece of evidence for the report's 'the numbers hold' thesis, and it is currently invisible.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 6, 'the mature exploratory landscape analysis tradition has never been pointed at surrogate-class choice'; and (iii) RANK 9 item 1 / the closing paragraph's Xu recommendation
findings.issue: Two interim notes attach explicit confidence downgrades and a named unread lead to positions the draft states flatly. The audit's own credibility posture -- it withdraws five of its own findings in section G -- makes unflagged over-statement here costlier than usual.
findings.evidence: interim-report-landscape-predicts-which-surrogate-wins.md, Confidence: 'high on the negative result... medium on the "no prior work targets surrogate-class selection via landscape" claim (five sources checked, two surveys with zero "surrogate" hits, one near-miss found and read in full - but the citation-chain lead to Yu et al. 2016 was not read directly, so I cannot rule out a specific niche precedent with full certainty).' Evidence weight adds: 'Rodriguez et al. 2024 is a genuine near-miss that partially cuts against a strong version of "nobody has looked at surrogate landscapes," so I have downgraded my language from "no one" to "no one in this exact offline-MBO, one-shot, GP-vs-ensemble framing."' interim-report-ntk-width-citations-never-verified.md, Confidence: 'medium-high for the Xu-compatibility verdict (the logical argument is sound... but no experiment in the paper or corpus directly measures whether the width-96 ensemble is already "NTK-regime-like" - that is an assumption, not a demonstrated fact).'
findings.recommendation: Carry the investigator's own downgraded phrasing: 'never pointed at surrogate-class choice in this exact offline, one-shot, GP-versus-ensemble framing', with Yu et al. 2016 named as the unread lead at the point of the claim rather than only in the terminal section. For Xu, add the note's stated assumption -- that the width-96 ensemble is already approximately NTK-regime is assumed, not demonstrated -- and name the falsifier the note supplies: an R-squared ray-extrapolation diagnostic (ensemble-mean versus GP-mean linear fit along rays from the data centroid) run on the paper's actual trained checkpoints, which is the experiment that would upgrade the compatibility verdict from logically sound to empirically confirmed.

findings.location: N6 section D, ground (1) row ('SURVIVES, now with domain support') and ground (2) row's phrase 'genuinely aliased in the strict design-of-experiments sense [13]'
findings.issue: The draft cites the NIST handbook twice as bare authority without the two sentences that make the ground-(1) criterion honest rather than convenient. The interim note's key move is a concession the draft never makes.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n6-residual-scoping-legitimate-or-gerrymandered.md quotes NIST 5.3.2 verbatim -- factor identification is 'Guidelines to assist the engineering judgment process of selecting process variables for a DOE... Include all important factors (based on engineering judgment)' -- and concludes: 'DOE theory itself explicitly delegates factor identification to domain judgment - it does not derive a rule for what counts as "the same factor" from statistical first principles, so ground (1) was never going to find an abstract mathematical arbiter. What it can find, and does, is *domain* precedent.' Separately, NIST 5.3.3.4.3 verbatim: 'Confounding means we have lost the ability to estimate some effects and/or interactions', with the note's gloss that 'confounding is a property of a design's contrast structure - two effects are aliased when they cannot be run apart, not when an author merely chooses to call them "the same factor."'
findings.recommendation: In ground (1), state the concession first -- no statistical theory adjudicates what counts as a factor; NIST 5.3.2 explicitly assigns that to domain judgment -- and then present the Abdar/Li-Rudner-Wilson domain precedent as the right kind of warrant. Conceding that there is no abstract arbiter is what stops the criterion reading as constructed for the occasion. In ground (2), quote the NIST aliasing definition so 'aliased in the strict sense' is a test the reader can apply to CbAS and MINs rather than a label.

findings.location: (i) G, the paragraph 'Three of the four citations verify clean, and the audit should say so', specifically 'The one elided nuance: Lee 2019's own text notes the gradient-descent-limit GP is "noticeably different" from the NNGP Bayesian posterior'
findings.issue: The draft names one nuance in the kernel-limit cluster where the interim note found two, and the omitted one is a self-disclaimer by the cited paper against the exact inference the audited paper draws.
findings.evidence: interim-report-ntk-width-citations-never-verified.md, source 2: Lee et al. 2018 'explicitly declines to claim SGD-trained finite networks converge to GP behavior: "Whether gradient-based stochastic optimization implements an approximate Bayesian computation is an interesting question... Further investigation is needed to determine if SGD does approximately implement Bayesian inference."' The note also flags an order-of-limits caveat -- Lee 2018's derivation takes widths to infinity sequentially, crediting the simultaneous case to Matthews et al. 2018 -- and records Jacot's own Section 6.1 finite-width ablation as directly on-point evidence: 'For the wider network, the NTK shows less variance and is smoother... this effect is much less apparent for the wider network (n=10000) than for the smaller network (n=500).'
findings.recommendation: Add Lee 2018's own disclaimer alongside the Lee 2019 'noticeably different' nuance -- the PASS verdict is more credible when it names every caveat the sources themselves raise, and this one shows the audit read past the abstract. Optionally add Jacot's Section 6.1 n=500-versus-n=10000 ablation as the one place in the cited cluster where a finite-width effect is actually measured, which is directly relevant to the paper's 96-to-1024 sweep.
